name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
issuer: the Saint Christopher and Nevis Inland Revenue Department (SKNIRD)
note: Saint Kitts and Nevis's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; saved in wave 7, the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30. The TIN is issued solely by the Saint Christopher and Nevis Inland Revenue Department (SKNIRD), to an individual or entity on registration if liable for the licences and taxes it administers; it isn't issued automatically to residents (individuals only once registered for an IRD licence or liable to an IRD tax). So it is given on registration, to anyone so liable ('anyone': the sheet sets no citizenship or residence for individuals). It is generated by the tax system, numeric, 'from one digit upwards' with no most: `min` 1 and no `length` (the form's way since 2026-10-30), the pattern digits only. A tax account number adds a two-digit tax-type code, and a VAT TIN one digit, neither held; the TIN also leads a driver's licence number, not modelled. The sheet names no age, fee or time, and doesn't say in words what needs one, so `needed` is left out.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Saint Kitts and Nevis: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: A Tax Identification Number (TIN) is issued solely by the jurisdiction’s Tax Administration, Saint Christopher and Nevis Inland Revenue Department (SKNIRD). ... An individual or legal person or legal entity will be issued a TIN upon registration if they are liable for the licences and taxes administered by the SKNIRD. ... Individuals No Entities No ... Individuals are only provided with a TIN if they are registered for one of the licences issued by the IRD or are liable to taxes administered by the IRD. ... TINs are automatically generated by the Tax Administration System and are numeric in structure but can range from one digit upwards.
